source.title: Standard Treatment Guidelines for General Hospitals, Fourth Edition
source.source_status: User-provided national guideline; source text summarized, not reproduced verbatim.

intended_use: Reference structure for later clinician-reviewed clinical decision-support development.

safety.emergency_rule: If any danger sign or hemodynamic instability is present, prioritize immediate emergency assessment/referral; do not wait for the software output.

global_danger_signs: severe respiratory distress or oxygen saturation below 90%
ongoing or severe chest pain suggestive of acute coronary syndrome
hemodynamically unstable tachyarrhythmia or symptomatic severe bradycardia

conditions.name: Cardiac arrhythmias
key_assessment: 12-lead ECG is the main diagnostic test
Consider electrolytes, thyroid function, CBC, echocardiography and chest X-ray guided by clinical findings
safety_rules: Do not initiate antiarrhythmic medication without ECG confirmation
Treat wide-complex tachycardia as potentially ventricular until assessed by an appropriately trained clinician

conditions.name: Adult hypertension
key_assessment: Measure blood pressure correctly and repeat as appropriate
Assess cardiovascular risk and target-organ damage
Check renal function and other tests as clinically indicated
reference_thresholds_from_STG: Adult hypertension threshold stated as BP at or above 140/90 mmHg
Severe BP alone does not define hypertensive emergency; acute target-organ damage is required
safety_rules: Pregnancy or possible pregnancy changes medicine selection
Avoid ACE inhibitors, ARBs and thiazides in pregnancy; seek appropriate clinician review
Suspected hypertensive emergency requires urgent hospital-level assessment

conditions.name: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease / coronary syndromes
suggestive_features: acute or persistent chest pain may indicate ACS
key_assessment: further cardiac testing or referral when indicated
urgent_escalation: Suspected acute coronary syndrome is a medical emergency and requires urgent hospital assessment

conditions.name: Rheumatic heart disease
key_assessment: assess complications and need for specialist care
safety_rules: Suspected significant valve disease or heart failure requires clinician assessment and referral

conditions.name: Valvular heart disease
key_assessment: Echocardiography to define valve lesion and cardiac function
urgent_escalation: acute valve dysfunction with shock, cyanosis or pulmonary edema is an emergency
safety_rules: STG recommends specialist/cardiologist consultation or referral for important valve lesions

conditions.name: Infective endocarditis
suggestive_features: unexplained fever with a new heart murmur
known damaged or prosthetic valve with systemic illness
key_assessment: blood cultures before antibiotics when feasible and without delaying emergency care
echocardiography and other investigations as available
safety_rules: Maintain high suspicion when new murmur accompanies unexplained fever or bacteremia
Requires hospital-level evaluation and specialist input

pediatric_scope_note: This dataset is Chapter 4 cardiovascular disorders and should not be treated as complete pediatric coverage. Pediatric cardiovascular content is addressed separately in STG Chapter 16.7 and requires a separate extraction and review.
next_development_step: Clinician review of this structured reference, then build explicit age-specific and condition-specific decision rules with test cases. Drug doses should be added only after independent verification and sign-off.
